variants.prompt: Which architecture are the hosts?

default.label: x86_64
default.summary: amd64. Every machine pool must use the same architecture.

variants.defaultRationale: The agent-based parameter table lists amd64, arm64, ppc64le, and s390x, and mixed architectures are not supported.

alternatives.label: ARM 64-bit
alternatives.summary: arm64 for every pool.

alternatives.label: IBM Power
alternatives.summary: ppc64le for every pool.

alternatives.label: IBM Z or LinuxONE
alternatives.summary: s390x. ISO boot is only supported on KVM. z/VM and LPAR boot with PXE.

variants.prompt: Which platform value will install-config.yaml use for these bare metal hosts?

default.label: baremetal
default.summary: platform.baremetal. Day-2 provisioning fields can be set now so you do not have to add them later.

variants.defaultRationale: The parameter guide lists baremetal as a platform. Its bare metal table is not used to boot the agent ISO, but it is there for the cluster after installation.

alternatives.label: none
alternatives.summary: platform.none. You provide API and ingress load balancers yourself, except on single-node OpenShift.

variants.prompt: How many control plane and compute nodes will the cluster have?

default.label: High availability with workers
default.summary: 3 control plane nodes and the default of 3 workers. controlPlane.replicas may also be 4 or 5.

variants.defaultRationale: Supported control plane replica counts are 3, 4, 5, or 1. The compute replica default is 3.

alternatives.label: Three-node compact
alternatives.summary: 3 control plane nodes and 0 workers. Ingress pods run on the control plane.

alternatives.label: Single-node OpenShift
alternatives.summary: controlPlane.replicas is 1 and there are no workers.

alternatives.label: Two-node with an arbiter
alternatives.summary: arbiter.replicas is 1. ZTP is not supported for two-node clusters with fencing.

variants.prompt: Can the hosts pull release images from the internet?

default.label: Connected
default.summary: Hosts can reach the registries named in the pull secret.
default.example: The sample install-config.yaml has no imageContentSources field.

variants.defaultRationale: A disconnected install has to mirror the release images first. A connected install does not.

alternatives.label: Disconnected or restricted
alternatives.summary: Mirror the OpenShift images into a registry the hosts can reach.

variants.prompt: Where do the hosts get the OpenShift release images?

default.label: Pull from the public registries
default.summary: Use the pull secret from the Hybrid Cloud Console. No mirror registry.

variants.defaultRationale: Connected installs authenticate to the public registries with the pull secret.

alternatives.label: Self-contained media, no external registry
alternatives.summary: Technology Preview. The media includes a virtualization operator bundle and no storage operators.
alternatives.example: You do not need to configure an external image registry.

citations.locator: Chapter 5. Installing a cluster without an external registry

variants.prompt: How will a disconnected environment get the release images?

default.label: Mirror registry
default.summary: Mirror the images, then set imageContentSources from the mirror command output.

variants.defaultRationale: Chapter 2 says a disconnected install on infrastructure you provision must mirror the images before installation.

alternatives.label: Self-contained media, no external registry
alternatives.summary: Technology Preview. Skips the mirror registry. Storage operators are not in the bundle.
alternatives.example: The installation ISO includes the OpenShift release images.

variants.prompt: Which command builds the mirror that imageContentSources will point at?

default.label: oc-mirror plugin v2
default.summary: The supported way to mirror the release. Copy its output into imageContentSources.

variants.defaultRationale: oc adm release mirror is deprecated in 4.22. The guide tells you to use oc-mirror plugin v2 instead.

alternatives.label: oc adm release mirror
alternatives.summary: Deprecated in 4.22 and planned for removal. Still documented as a source of imageContentSources text.

citations.locator: 2.2. About mirroring the OpenShift Container Platform image repository

variants.prompt: How does the cluster trust the mirror registry?

default.label: additionalTrustBundle
default.summary: Paste the mirror CA or self-signed certificate into additionalTrustBundle.

variants.defaultRationale: The disconnected procedure says to add that certificate when the mirror is not already trusted.

citations.locator: Chapter 2. additionalTrustBundle for the mirror registry

variants.prompt: Do the hosts reach Red Hat services directly?

default.label: Direct
default.summary: No proxy in front of the sites the cluster must reach.
default.example: The sample install-config.yaml has no proxy field.

variants.defaultRationale: The preparing steps say to configure a firewall or proxy only when one sits between the hosts and the required sites.

alternatives.label: Proxy or firewall
alternatives.summary: The hosts go through a proxy or firewall. It must allow the sites the cluster needs.
alternatives.example: If you use a firewall or proxy, you configured it to allow the sites that your cluster requires access to.

variants.prompt: Does the proxy present a certificate the nodes do not already trust?

default.label: Already trusted
default.summary: No extra bundle.

variants.defaultRationale: additionalTrustBundle is how a proxy certificate is added to the nodes' trust store when one is required.

alternatives.label: Add additionalTrustBundle
alternatives.summary: PEM bundle added to the nodes' trusted certificate store.

variants.prompt: How will the hosts boot the agent?

default.label: Full ISO
default.summary: minimalISO is false. The ISO contains the rootfs.

variants.defaultRationale: minimalISO defaults to false, so the generated image is a full ISO.

alternatives.label: Minimal ISO
alternatives.summary: minimalISO is true. The ISO does not contain the rootfs image.

alternatives.label: PXE or iPXE
alternatives.summary: The installer uploads PXE assets to the bootArtifactsBaseURL server.

variants.prompt: The ISO boot is only supported when the s390x host is KVM. What is the host?

default.label: RHEL KVM
default.summary: ISO or PXE is allowed.

variants.defaultRationale: The preparing chapter says ISO boot on s390x is only for RHEL KVM. z/VM and LPAR use PXE.

alternatives.label: z/VM or LPAR
alternatives.summary: Switch the boot media to PXE. ISO boot is not supported here.

variants.prompt: Where will PXE clients download the boot assets?

default.label: Set bootArtifactsBaseURL
default.summary: URL of the server that serves the PXE assets.

variants.defaultRationale: For an iPXE script, bootArtifactsBaseURL is the server the installer uploads PXE assets to.

variants.prompt: Where does the minimal ISO pull the rootfs?

default.label: Embedded public URL
default.summary: Leave bootArtifactsBaseURL empty. The installer embeds a URL that needs internet access.

variants.defaultRationale: On a connected network the embedded rootfs URL is the default when minimalISO is true.

alternatives.label: Set bootArtifactsBaseURL
alternatives.summary: Point the minimal ISO at your own rootfs URL.

variants.prompt: Where does the minimal ISO pull the rootfs when the network is disconnected?

default.label: Set bootArtifactsBaseURL
default.summary: The embedded URL needs the internet. A disconnected install has to provide its own rootfs URL.

variants.defaultRationale: The embedded rootfs URL is only described as usable when the environment has an internet connection.

variants.prompt: Which address family will the cluster network use?

default.label: IPv4
default.summary: Single-stack IPv4. Do not install this on a host that is itself dual-stack.

variants.defaultRationale: The network section says not to install a single-stack IPv4 cluster on a dual-stack host, and it documents IPv4, IPv6, and dual-stack.

alternatives.label: IPv6
alternatives.summary: Single-stack IPv6. networkType stays OVNKubernetes.

alternatives.label: Dual-stack
alternatives.summary: IPv4 and IPv6 on the same default-gateway NIC, listed in the same order everywhere.
alternatives.example:
clusterNetwork:
- cidr: 10.128.0.0/14
  hostPrefix: 23
- cidr: fd00:10:128::/56
  hostPrefix: 64
serviceNetwork:
- 172.30.0.0/16
- fd00:172:16::/112

variants.prompt: How will you order the two address families?

default.label: IPv4 before IPv6 on one NIC
default.summary: Same NIC for both default gateways. The same order in clusterNetwork, serviceNetwork, and machineNetwork.
default.example:
clusterNetwork:
- cidr: 10.128.0.0/14
  hostPrefix: 23
- cidr: fd00:10:128::/56
  hostPrefix: 64
serviceNetwork:
- 172.30.0.0/16
- fd00:172:16::/112

variants.defaultRationale: Both families must use the same default-gateway interface, and every network list must use the same family order.

alternatives.label: IPv6 before IPv4 on one NIC
alternatives.summary: Same rules, with IPv6 listed first in every network parameter.
alternatives.example: If you specified the DualStackIPv6Primary parameter, you must list the IPv6 address first.

variants.prompt: How do the hosts get their IP addresses?

default.label: DHCP
default.summary: Leave networkConfig empty. rendezvousIP must be an address of a host that will be a control plane node.

variants.defaultRationale: The preparing chapter shows DHCP with an empty networkConfig and a rendezvous IP chosen before the ISO is built.

alternatives.label: Static NMState
alternatives.summary: Write networkConfig for each host. It is one NMState desired state. Interfaces in that state can use a static address, DHCP, or no address, and several interface types can sit in the same block.
alternatives.example:
ipv4:
  address:
  - ip: 192.168.111.80
    prefix-length: 23
  dhcp: false

variants.prompt: Which address is the rendezvous host?

default.label: A future control plane DHCP address
default.summary: Set rendezvousIP before you generate the ISO. Every host checks in to the service on that address.

variants.defaultRationale: With DHCP, rendezvousIP has to be known when the ISO is generated, and it has to belong to a host that will join the control plane.

variants.prompt: How is the rendezvous IP chosen when addresses are static?

default.label: Set rendezvousIP
default.summary: Put the rendezvous address in agent-config.yaml.

variants.defaultRationale: If you omit rendezvousIP, one address is taken from the hosts' networkConfig. You must set it when no host IP is in networkConfig.

alternatives.label: Select it from networkConfig
alternatives.summary: Omit rendezvousIP and let the installer pick an address that networkConfig already has.

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include an ethernet interface?

default.label: Include ethernet
default.summary: type ethernet. Set state to up when IPv4 and IPv6 are both disabled, or the interface can still receive a DHCP address.

variants.defaultRationale: The NMState book defines ethernet as an interface type in the node desired state. Bond, VLAN, Linux bridge, VRF, and InfiniBand are other types in that same state. SR-IOV is ethernet.sr-iov on the physical function.

alternatives.label: No ethernet interface
alternatives.summary: Leave type ethernet out of this networkConfig.

citations.locator: 1.9.1. Example: Ethernet interface node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: How does NMState find that interface?

default.label: Interface name
default.summary: identifier name applies the configuration to the interface with that name. name is the default.

variants.defaultRationale: The NMState book lists identifier values name, mac-address, and pci-address. name is the default. A wrong MAC is an invalid argument. A PCI address uses domain:bus:device.function.

alternatives.label: MAC address
alternatives.summary: identifier mac-address, with mac-address set. The name can still be set, and the MAC is the primary identifier.

alternatives.label: PCI address
alternatives.summary: identifier pci-address, with pci-address set. The address matches the hardware slot, which stays put when the kernel name changes.

variants.prompt: Will this interface carry alt-names?

default.label: No alt-names
default.summary: Use the kernel interface name only.

variants.defaultRationale: alt-names are optional labels, up to 127 characters, and they can be used as bond ports, VLAN base interfaces, bridge ports, and route next hops. They cannot be set on br-ex or on interfaces associated with br-ex.

alternatives.label: Set alt-names
alternatives.summary: Add alt-names on the interface. Applying the same names again leaves the configuration unchanged.

variants.prompt: Does this ethernet interface create SR-IOV virtual functions?

default.label: No SR-IOV
default.summary: Leave ethernet.sr-iov off this interface.

variants.defaultRationale: SR-IOV is ethernet.sr-iov on a type ethernet interface. A bond is a separate type. The NMState book also describes bonding those virtual functions, which is the bond decision.

alternatives.label: Set ethernet.sr-iov
alternatives.summary: Create virtual functions on this physical function. If the SR-IOV Network Operator also manages the physical function, set externallyManaged on the SriovNetworkNodePolicy.
alternatives.example:
ethernet:
  sr-iov:
    total-vfs: 3
    vfs:
    - id: 0
      max-tx-rate: 200

citations.locator: 1.9.6. Example: Node network configuration policy for virtual functions

variants.prompt: Which ethernet.sr-iov fields do you set?

default.label: Set total-vfs and the per-VF fields you need
default.summary: ethernet.sr-iov.total-vfs is the number of virtual functions. Each entry in vfs can set id, max-tx-rate, trust, and vlan-id.

variants.defaultRationale: The NMState virtual-function policy defines total-vfs, vfs.id, vfs.max-tx-rate, vfs.trust, and vfs.vlan-id on the physical function.

citations.locator: 1.9.6. Example: Node network configuration policy for virtual functions

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include a bond?

default.label: No bond
default.summary: Leave type bond out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: A bond is type bond with link-aggregation.port listing the subordinate interfaces. It can share a desired state with a VLAN or with SR-IOV virtual functions.

alternatives.label: NIC bond
alternatives.summary: type bond. Optional mtu defaults to 1500. Optional link-aggregation.options.miimon sets how often the bond link is inspected.

citations.locator: 1.9.4. Example: Bond interface node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Which link-aggregation.mode does the bond use?

default.label: active-backup
default.summary: No switch configuration. This is the only bond mode that can attach an IP over InfiniBand interface. options.primary is valid in this mode.

variants.defaultRationale: OpenShift supports active-backup, balance-xor, and 802.3ad. Other bond modes are not supported. active-backup does not require switch configuration.

alternatives.label: balance-xor
alternatives.summary: Requires switch EtherChannel or a similar port group, plus load-balancing configuration for the traffic.

alternatives.label: 802.3ad
alternatives.summary: Requires switch EtherChannel or a similar port group, plus load-balancing configuration for the traffic.

citations.locator: 1.9.4. Example: Bond interface node network configuration policy
1.10. Creating an IP over InfiniBand interface on nodes

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include a VLAN interface?

default.label: No VLAN
default.summary: Leave type vlan out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: A VLAN is type vlan. On bare metal the interface name must be parent.vlanid. Put the VLAN and its routes in the same desired state, because policy order is not guaranteed across separate manifests.

alternatives.label: VLAN
alternatives.summary: type vlan, with vlan.base-iface and vlan.id. The name is parent.vlanid.
alternatives.example:
name: eth1.102
type: vlan
vlan:
  base-iface: eth1
  id: 102

citations.locator: 1.9.3. Example: VLAN interface node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Which VLAN id goes on the parent interface?

default.label: Set vlan.id
default.summary: vlan.base-iface is the parent NIC or bond. vlan.id is the tag. On bare metal the interface name is parent.vlanid.
default.example:
name: eth1.102
vlan:
  base-iface: eth1
  id: 102

variants.defaultRationale: The VLAN policy sets vlan.base-iface and vlan.id. Bare metal accepts only the parent.vlanid name.

citations.locator: 1.9.3. Example: VLAN interface node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include a Linux bridge?

default.label: No Linux bridge
default.summary: Leave type linux-bridge out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: A Linux bridge is type linux-bridge. bridge.port names the attached NICs. bridge.options.stp.enabled turns spanning tree on or off. This is the kernel bridge, separate from the OVN br-ex bridge.

alternatives.label: Linux bridge
alternatives.summary: type linux-bridge, with bridge.port and bridge.options.stp.enabled.

citations.locator: 1.9.2. Example: Linux bridge interface node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include a VRF?

default.label: No VRF
default.summary: Leave type vrf out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: A VRF is type vrf. vrf.port lists the interfaces in the instance. vrf.route-table-id must be lower than 1000, because 1000 and above are reserved for OpenShift.

alternatives.label: VRF
alternatives.summary: type vrf, with vrf.port and vrf.route-table-id.

citations.locator: 1.9.7. Example: Network interface with a VRF instance node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Which route table does the VRF use?

default.label: route-table-id below 1000
default.summary: vrf.route-table-id must be lower than 1000. OpenShift reserves 1000 and above.

variants.defaultRationale: The VRF policy says a route table id of 1000 or higher is reserved for OpenShift Container Platform.

citations.locator: 1.9.7. Example: Network interface with a VRF instance node network configuration policy

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig include an InfiniBand interface?

default.label: No InfiniBand
default.summary: Leave type infiniband out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: An IPoIB interface is type infiniband, with infiniband.mode and infiniband.pkey. Attaching it to a bond is supported only in active-backup mode. The MAC is a 20-byte string when identifier is mac-address.

alternatives.label: InfiniBand
alternatives.summary: type infiniband. Set infiniband.pkey. None and 0xffff are the base-interface protection keys.

citations.locator: 1.10. Creating an IP over InfiniBand interface on nodes

variants.prompt: Which infiniband.mode does the interface use?

default.label: datagram
default.summary: The default IPoIB mode.

variants.defaultRationale: datagram is the default. connected is supported when you need to change the MTU so the node can reach surrounding devices.

alternatives.label: connected
alternatives.summary: Use connected when the MTU has to change for connectivity with surrounding devices.

citations.locator: 1.10. Creating an IP over InfiniBand interface on nodes

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig set dns-resolver?

default.label: No dns-resolver
default.summary: Leave DNS to DHCP or to the host default.

variants.defaultRationale: dns-resolver.config holds server, search, and options for the node. NMState stores DNS globally by default. Storing DNS on an interface can break resolution after that interface joins a bridge or a bond.

alternatives.label: Set dns-resolver
alternatives.summary: dns-resolver.config.server, search, and options. An empty config clears DNS options.

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig set routes?

default.label: No static routes
default.summary: Leave routes out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: routes.config entries set destination, next-hop-interface, next-hop-address, metric, and table-id. To replace a route, mark the old one state absent and the new one state present. state ignore leaves a route alone. br-ex cannot be the next hop unless that bridge was customized.

alternatives.label: Set routes
alternatives.summary: Add routes.config. The next hop must be in the same subnet as the interface address.

variants.prompt: Does networkConfig set route-rules?

default.label: No route rules
default.summary: Leave route-rules out of this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: route-rules.config is policy routing. ip-from selects the source, priority orders the rule, and route-table names the table that handles the match.

alternatives.label: Set route-rules
alternatives.summary: route-rules.config with ip-from, priority, and route-table.

variants.prompt: Does an interface set ipv4.forwarding?

default.label: Leave forwarding unset
default.summary: Do not set ipv4.forwarding in this networkConfig.

variants.defaultRationale: ipv4.forwarding enables IPv4 forwarding on that interface. The NMState operator configures IPv4 only. The interface can be a physical NIC, a bond, or a VLAN.

alternatives.label: Enable ipv4.forwarding
alternatives.summary: Set ipv4.enabled and ipv4.forwarding on the interface that should forward IPv4 packets.

citations.locator: 1.13. Enable IP forwarding on specific interfaces

variants.prompt: Which interface names does this networkConfig avoid?

default.label: Avoid the reserved names
default.summary: Do not use br-ext, br-int, br-local, br-nexthop, br0, ext-vxlan, ext, genev_sys_*, int, k8s-*, ovn-k8s-*, patch-br-*, tun0, or vxlan_sys_*.

variants.defaultRationale: The NMState policy chapter reserves those names. An existing br-ex bridge, and interfaces associated with it, cannot be modified except through a customized br-ex manifest.

variants.prompt: Will you keep the default pod, service, and machine networks?

default.label: Keep the defaults
default.summary: Pods 10.128.0.0/14 with hostPrefix 23, services 172.30.0.0/16, machines 10.0.0.0/16. networkType is OVNKubernetes. The join subnet stays 100.64.0.0/16.

variants.defaultRationale: Those are the defaults in the network parameter table, and you cannot change the networking object after installation.

alternatives.label: Set your own CIDRs
alternatives.summary: Replace clusterNetwork, serviceNetwork, or machineNetwork. They must not overlap, and machineNetwork must match the preferred NIC.

variants.prompt: Did you keep the custom CIDRs away from the ranges OpenShift already uses?

default.label: Checked
default.summary: machineNetwork does not include Podman's 10.88.0.0/16 bridge. The OVN join subnet does not overlap any node network and is larger than the node count.
default.example: Do not set machineNetwork.cidr to include 10.88.0.0/16. The internalJoinSubnet default is 100.64.0.0/16.

variants.defaultRationale: The preparing chapter says a machineNetwork that includes 10.88.0.0/16 fails the install. The join subnet cannot be changed later.

variants.prompt: Install with FIPS mode enabled?

default.label: Leave fips false
default.summary: The default is false.

variants.defaultRationale: fips defaults to false. Turning it on requires the installer to run on a RHEL host that is already in FIPS mode, and it cannot be enabled after the first boot.

alternatives.label: fips true
alternatives.summary: Run openshift-install on a FIPS-enabled RHEL host. Supported on x86_64, ppc64le, and s390x.

variants.prompt: Which optional components ship with the cluster?

default.label: vCurrent
default.summary: baselineCapabilitySet defaults to vCurrent.

variants.defaultRationale: Valid baselines are None, v4.11, v4.12, and vCurrent. The default is vCurrent.

alternatives.label: None
alternatives.summary: Start with no optional capabilities and add only what you list.

alternatives.label: v4.11
alternatives.summary: The v4.11 baseline set.

alternatives.label: v4.12
alternatives.summary: The v4.12 baseline set.

variants.prompt: Add capabilities beyond the baseline?

default.label: No additionalEnabledCapabilities
default.summary: The baseline alone.

variants.defaultRationale: additionalEnabledCapabilities is optional and extends the baseline.

alternatives.label: List additionalEnabledCapabilities
alternatives.summary: Name the extra optional components to install with the cluster.

variants.prompt: Reserve CPUs for OpenShift services?

default.label: cpuPartitioningMode None
default.summary: The default. Workload partitioning stays off.

variants.defaultRationale: You can only enable workload partitioning at install, and you cannot turn it off later. None is the default.

alternatives.label: AllNodes
alternatives.summary: Isolate platform workloads onto reserved CPUs on every node. This does not by itself pin your application CPUs.

variants.prompt: Leave simultaneous multithreading enabled?

default.label: Enabled
default.summary: The default for control plane and compute pools.

variants.defaultRationale: Hyperthreading is enabled by default. Disabling it cuts machine capacity and has to be planned for.

alternatives.label: Disabled
alternatives.summary: Set hyperthreading to Disabled on the control plane and compute pools.

variants.prompt: Will you put an SSH public key in install-config.yaml?

default.label: Provide sshKey
default.summary: Needed for installation debugging and disaster recovery on a production cluster.

variants.defaultRationale: The parameter note says to set an SSH key on production clusters where you may need to debug the install or recover a node.

alternatives.label: Omit sshKey
alternatives.summary: The field is optional. You will not have that login on the hosts.

variants.prompt: Add NTP servers beyond what the hosts already use?

default.label: No additionalNTPSources
default.summary: Hosts keep the NTP configuration they already have.

variants.defaultRationale: additionalNTPSources is optional and is added on top of NTP sources configured another way.

alternatives.label: List additionalNTPSources
alternatives.summary: Hostnames or IP addresses added to every cluster host.
alternatives.example: additionalNTPSources is a list of hostnames or IP addresses.

variants.prompt: Who assigns master and worker roles?

default.label: Let the installer assign roles
default.summary: Omit hosts.role. Roles are assigned during installation. The host count still cannot exceed controlPlane.replicas plus compute.replicas.

variants.defaultRationale: If agent-config.yaml does not set a role, the installer assigns master or worker during the install.

alternatives.label: Pin each host's role
alternatives.summary: Set hosts.role to master or worker, and set hostname if DHCP or reverse DNS is not enough.

variants.prompt: Which disk gets RHCOS?

default.label: First matching disk the installer finds
default.summary: Omit rootDeviceHints.

variants.defaultRationale: rootDeviceHints is optional. Without it the installer does not target a specific device.

alternatives.label: Set rootDeviceHints
alternatives.summary: The installer uses the first discovered device that matches every hint you set.

variants.prompt: Which hint identifies the install disk?

default.label: deviceName by path
default.summary: Prefer /dev/disk/by-path/... The hint must match exactly.

variants.defaultRationale: The hint table says to prefer the by-path device name. Hints can be combined, and the device must match all of them.

alternatives.label: wwn
alternatives.summary: Unique storage identifier. If udevadm prints ID_WWN_WITH_EXTENSION, use that value.
alternatives.example: wwn is the ID_WWN_WITH_EXTENSION value when udevadm prints one.

alternatives.label: serialNumber
alternatives.summary: Exact serial number.
alternatives.example: serialNumber matches the device serial number exactly.

alternatives.label: hctl
alternatives.summary: SCSI address such as 0:0:0:0. Exact match.

alternatives.label: model or vendor
alternatives.summary: A substring match on the model or the vendor name.
alternatives.example: model is a vendor-specific device identifier and can be a substring.

alternatives.label: minSizeGigabytes or rotational
alternatives.summary: Minimum size in gigabytes, or whether the disk must be rotational.

variants.prompt: How will you load balance the API and application ingress?

default.label: One load balancer
default.summary: The documented example uses one HAProxy for API ports 6443 and 22623 and ingress ports 80 and 443. A compact cluster must send ingress to the control plane nodes.

variants.defaultRationale: platform none requires you to provision API and ingress load balancers before installation, except for single-node OpenShift. Production clusters can split them.

alternatives.label: Separate API and ingress balancers
alternatives.summary: Scale the API and application ingress load balancers independently. API balancing stays layer 4 and stateless.

variants.prompt: Will the cluster manage a provisioning network after installation?

default.label: Managed
default.summary: The default. The cluster runs DHCP and TFTP for the provisioning network.

variants.defaultRationale: provisioningNetwork defaults to Managed. These fields are for after the agent install, so setting them now avoids a day-2 edit.

alternatives.label: Disabled
alternatives.summary: No provisioning network. Later hosts are added with virtual media, and BMCs must be reachable on the bare-metal network.

decisions.title: Provisioning services without a provisioning network

variants.prompt: Where do the provisioning services listen?

default.label: Two addresses on the bare-metal network
default.summary: Provide two bare-metal IPs for the provisioning services. Day-2 provisioning is virtual media only.
default.example: You must provide two IP addresses on the bare-metal network.

variants.defaultRationale: When provisioningNetwork is Disabled, the table requires those two addresses, and virtual media is the only day-2 provisioning method.

variants.prompt: When will you record BMC addresses for the hosts?

default.label: Leave them for day 2
default.summary: platform.baremetal.hosts is not used to boot the agent ISO.

variants.defaultRationale: The bare metal table says these fields are not used for the initial provision. They exist so you can set them at install time instead of coming back later.

alternatives.label: Set them in install-config.yaml now
alternatives.summary: Record bootMACAddress, BMC address URL, username, and password. Set disableCertificateVerification when the BMC certificate is self-signed. The address URL includes the protocol, for example redfish.

variants.prompt: After installation, do you keep the default OVS br-ex bridge?

default.label: Keep the default bridge
default.summary: One NIC and the standard OVS settings. OpenShift configures br-ex for you.
default.example: OpenShift Container Platform automatically configures the br-ex bridge.

variants.defaultRationale: Chapter 10 says the default bridge is for a single NIC and standard OVS settings. Customizing it is a post-install step.

alternatives.label: Custom NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy
alternatives.summary: Override br-ex for MTU, DNS, bond attributes, or LLDP. Copy the full install NMState into the policy or the node can lose its network.
alternatives.example:
kind: NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy
name: br-ex
type: ovs-bridge

variants.prompt: The custom bridge is applied by the Kubernetes NMState Operator. Is it installed?

default.label: Install the NMState Operator
default.summary: Required before the NodeNetworkConfigurationPolicy. The policy's primary IP cannot be changed afterward.

variants.defaultRationale: Chapter 10 lists the NMState Operator as a prerequisite for the br-ex policy.

citations.locator: 10.1. Creating a manifest object that includes a customized br-ex bridge

variants.prompt: What are you changing on the bridge?

default.label: MTU
default.summary: Change the maximum transmission unit.
default.example: You need to modify the maximum transmission unit (MTU) for your cluster.

variants.defaultRationale: The post-install chapter lists MTU, DNS, bond attributes, and LLDP as the reasons to replace the default bridge.

alternatives.label: DNS
alternatives.summary: Update DNS values in the NMState policy.

alternatives.label: Bond mode, MIImon, or QoS
alternatives.summary: Change attributes of a bond that backs br-ex.

alternatives.label: LLDP
alternatives.summary: Enable Link Layer Discovery Protocol to troubleshoot the switch port.
alternatives.example: You need to enable Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) to discover and troubleshoot switch connectivity.

citations.locator: 10.1. Creating a manifest object that includes a customized br-ex bridge

variants.prompt: Which operators does the rendezvous console install with the cluster?

default.label: Virtualization bundle
default.summary: Select Virtualization in the Bundles section. This installs the operators the console recommends for virtual machines. This installation method is Technology Preview, and the bundle includes no storage operators.

variants.defaultRationale: Chapter 5 says to select Virtualization in the Bundles section when you want the operators recommended for virtual machines. The same chapter says the bundle includes no storage operators.

alternatives.label: Single operators
alternatives.summary: Select operators one by one in the Single Operators section. Some of those operators can be installed only as part of the Virtualization bundle. The 4.22 agent chapter does not print their names.

citations.locator: 5.4. Configuring cluster details and choosing Operators to install

variants.prompt: Will you add extra manifests in the openshift directory?

default.label: No extra manifests
default.summary: install-config.yaml and agent-config.yaml are enough. Extra manifests are optional.

variants.defaultRationale: Chapter 4 says additional manifests are optional. The installer does not validate them, and a bad manifest can leave the cluster unusable.

alternatives.label: Add manifests in the openshift directory
alternatives.summary: Put the files in <installation_directory>/openshift. The agent installer applies them when it creates the image. The most common kind is a MachineConfig. Chapter 8 also installs named operators from Subscription files in that directory.
alternatives.example:
<installation_directory>/openshift

kind: MachineConfig
name: 10-br-ex-worker
path: /etc/nmstate/openshift/worker-0.yml

kind: Subscription
name: multicluster-engine
channel: stable-2.3

kind: Subscription
name: local-storage-operator
installPlanApproval: Automatic

citations.locator: 4.5.1. Creating a directory to contain additional manifests
8.3. Preparing an Agent-based cluster deployment for the multicluster engine for Kubernetes Operator while connected

variants.prompt: After installation, which storage class will applications claim?

default.label: LVM Storage
default.summary: LVM Storage creates this class for device class vg1. The default reclaim policy is Delete and binding waits for the pod.
default.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: lvms-vg1
provisioner: topolvm.io
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
parameters:
  topolvm.io/device-class: vg1
  csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: xfs

variants.defaultRationale: The local storage chapter says device class vg1 creates the class lvms-vg1 with provisioner topolvm.io. This is a postinstallation choice. The cluster already runs on node disk.

alternatives.label: Local Storage Operator
alternatives.summary: The operator creates the class named local-sc. Local volumes are static, so the class uses the no-provisioner provisioner and does not create disks.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: local-sc
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner

alternatives.label: OpenShift Data Foundation
alternatives.summary: A bare metal Data Foundation cluster creates these classes. Ceph RBD is the block class you can set as the default. The bare metal guide also lists ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd
provisioner: openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true

kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: ocs-storagecluster-cephfs
provisioner: openshift-storage.cephfs.csi.ceph.com
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: true

kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: openshift-storage.noobaa.io
provisioner: openshift-storage.noobaa.io/obc
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate
allowVolumeExpansion: false

alternatives.label: hostPath for a test
alternatives.summary: The virtualization storage chapter creates this Hostpath Provisioner class. The local storage overview says upstream HostPath Provisioner is not recommended, and a hostPath volume is for a single-node test.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: hostpath-csi
provisioner: kubevirt.io.hostpath-provisioner
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  storagePool: my-storage-pool

variants.prompt: After installation, will applications also use an external storage class?

default.label: No external storage class
default.summary: The day-2 class above is enough. An external class is optional.

variants.defaultRationale: The postinstallation chapter says the cluster operates on ephemeral node storage until you configure persistent storage.

alternatives.label: Add an external storage class
alternatives.summary: You can add more than one. The virtualization chapter creates a SAN class from the LUNs you select. The CSI chapter creates an SMB class for a file share.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: filesystem1
provisioner: spectrumscale.csi.ibm.com

kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: samba
provisioner: smb.csi.k8s.io

citations.locator: 10.13.7. Creating a file system with Fusion Access for SAN

variants.prompt: After installation, will you add the SAN storage class?

default.label: No SAN storage class
default.summary: Leave the SAN class out. OpenShift does not ship a Fibre Channel or iSCSI StorageClass.

variants.defaultRationale: The virtualization chapter creates this class only after you build a file system from the LUNs you select.

alternatives.label: Include the SAN storage class
alternatives.summary: The class name is the file system name. The provisioner is spectrumscale.csi.ibm.com and volBackendFs matches that file system.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: filesystem1
provisioner: spectrumscale.csi.ibm.com
parameters:
  volBackendFs: filesystem1
reclaimPolicy: Delete
allowVolumeExpansion: true
volumeBindingMode: Immediate

citations.locator: 10.13.7. Creating a file system with Fusion Access for SAN

variants.prompt: After installation, will you add the SMB storage class?

default.label: No SMB storage class
default.summary: Leave the SMB class out. The book does not print an NFS StorageClass.

variants.defaultRationale: The CSI chapter creates this class when you want a share provisioned from an SMB server. NFS in the storage book is a static volume, not a storage class.

alternatives.label: Include the SMB storage class
alternatives.summary: The bound claim in the chapter uses the class name samba. The book leaves the server and share as placeholders and stores the credentials in the smbcreds secret.
alternatives.example:
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: samba
provisioner: smb.csi.k8s.io
parameters:
  source: //<hostname>/<shares>
  csi.storage.k8s.io/provisioner-secret-name: smbcreds
  csi.storage.k8s.io/provisioner-secret-namespace: samba-server
  csi.storage.k8s.io/node-stage-secret-name: smbcreds
  csi.storage.k8s.io/node-stage-secret-namespace: samba-server
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: Immediate

variants.prompt: After installation, where does the internal image registry store images?

default.label: Leave the registry Removed
default.summary: Bare metal does not provision registry storage. The operator stays Removed until you configure storage.

variants.defaultRationale: On platforms with no shareable object storage, the Image Registry Operator bootstraps as Removed so the install can finish.

alternatives.label: emptyDir for a non-production cluster
alternatives.summary: All images are lost if the registry pod restarts. This cannot be used with more than one replica.

alternatives.label: Persistent volume claim
alternatives.summary: Set managementState to Managed and leave spec.storage.pvc.claim blank. The operator creates the image-registry-storage claim. One replica uses ReadWriteOnce and the Recreate rollout. Plan for at least 100Gi. Two or more replicas need ReadWriteMany.
alternatives.example:
storage:
  pvc:
    claim:
managementState: Managed
PVC name created: image-registry-storage

alternatives.label: Data Foundation Ceph RGW
alternatives.summary: Create an ObjectBucketClaim on ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw, then point the registry at that bucket. The registry book recommends object storage ahead of a file claim.
alternatives.example:
kind: ObjectBucketClaim
name: rgwbucket
namespace: openshift-storage
storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rgw
generateBucketName: rgwbucket
secret: image-registry-private-configuration-user
region: us-east-1

alternatives.label: Data Foundation NooBaa
alternatives.summary: Create an ObjectBucketClaim on openshift-storage.noobaa.io. The route used for the endpoint is s3 in openshift-storage.
alternatives.example:
kind: ObjectBucketClaim
name: noobaatest
namespace: openshift-storage
storageClassName: openshift-storage.noobaa.io
generateBucketName: noobaatest
secret: image-registry-private-configuration-user
region: us-east-1

alternatives.label: Data Foundation CephFS claim
alternatives.summary: CephFS is a ReadWriteMany file claim. The registry book says not to use a PVC for the registry when Ceph RGW or NooBaa is available.
alternatives.example:
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
name: registry-storage-pvc
namespace: openshift-image-registry
accessModes: ReadWriteMany
storage: 100Gi
storageClassName: ocs-storagecluster-cephfs
claim: registry-storage-pvc

variants.prompt: After installation, will platform metrics and alerts survive a pod restart?

default.label: Leave monitoring on ephemeral storage
default.summary: A new cluster reports PrometheusDataPersistenceNotConfigured. Metrics and alert silences are lost when the pods restart.

variants.defaultRationale: Core monitoring starts without a volume claim. On a multi-node cluster the monitoring book says you must add persistent storage for Prometheus and Alertmanager.

alternatives.label: Persistent claims for Prometheus and Alertmanager
alternatives.summary: Add volumeClaimTemplate under prometheusK8s and alertmanagerMain in cluster-monitoring-config. Prometheus cannot use a raw block volume. If storageClassName is omitted, the default storage class is used.
alternatives.example:
kind: ConfigMap
name: cluster-monitoring-config
namespace: openshift-monitoring
prometheusK8s.volumeClaimTemplate
storageClassName: my-storage-class
storage: 40Gi
alertmanagerMain.volumeClaimTemplate

variants.prompt: After installation, will you monitor user projects?

default.label: Platform monitoring only
default.summary: User project monitoring stays off. Remove any custom Prometheus instances before you enable it later.

variants.defaultRationale: User workload monitoring is optional. The cluster administrator enables it in cluster-monitoring-config.

alternatives.label: Enable user project monitoring
alternatives.summary: Set enableUserWorkload to true. On a multi-node cluster, Prometheus, Alertmanager, and Thanos Ruler in the user workload stack also need persistent claims.
alternatives.example:
kind: ConfigMap
name: cluster-monitoring-config
namespace: openshift-monitoring
enableUserWorkload: true

variants.prompt: After you enable user project monitoring, where do those metrics live?

default.label: Leave user monitoring on ephemeral storage
default.summary: The user workload stack starts without a volume claim.

variants.defaultRationale: The user workload chapter says a multi-node cluster must give Prometheus, Alertmanager, and Thanos Ruler persistent storage.

alternatives.label: Persistent claim for Thanos Ruler
alternatives.summary: The printed sample is Thanos Ruler at 10Gi. Use the same volumeClaimTemplate shape for Prometheus and Alertmanager in user-workload-monitoring-config.
alternatives.example:
kind: ConfigMap
name: user-workload-monitoring-config
namespace: openshift-user-workload-monitoring
thanosRuler.volumeClaimTemplate
storageClassName: my-storage-class
storage: 10Gi

variants.prompt: After you enable user project monitoring, where do user alerts go?

default.label: Platform Alertmanager
default.summary: User alerts use the platform Alertmanager until you enable user routing.

variants.defaultRationale: If the dedicated user Alertmanager is omitted, user-defined alerts are routed to the platform Alertmanager.

alternatives.label: Let users route through the platform Alertmanager
alternatives.summary: Set enableUserAlertmanagerConfig so users can create AlertmanagerConfig objects against the platform instance.

alternatives.label: Dedicated Alertmanager for user projects
alternatives.summary: Start a separate Alertmanager in the user workload stack and let users define their own routes.

citations.locator: 1.3. Enabling alert routing for user-defined projects

variants.prompt: After installation, which log store will the cluster use?

default.label: No log store
default.summary: Logging is not part of the install. Cluster logs stay with the node until you install a log store.

variants.defaultRationale: The postinstallation storage table lists Loki and Elasticsearch as optional log stores you configure after the cluster exists.

alternatives.label: Loki on object storage
alternatives.summary: Loki is the current log store. Log chunks and indices go to S3-compatible object storage named in a secret. storageClassName is the block class for Loki internal volumes, not the object store. Block and file storage are not the log store.
alternatives.example:
apiVersion: loki.grafana.com/v1
kind: LokiStack
name: logging-loki
namespace: openshift-logging
size: 1x.small
storage.secret.name: logging-loki-s3
storage.secret.type: s3
storageClassName: <storage_class_name>
tenants.mode: openshift-logging

alternatives.label: Elasticsearch on block storage
alternatives.summary: The OpenShift Elasticsearch Operator is deprecated. Block storage is recommended. Object storage is not supported. NFS is not supported for this log store.
alternatives.example: Elasticsearch log store on block storage

variants.prompt: After installation, where do firing alerts go?

default.label: Alerting UI only
default.summary: Firing alerts show in the web console. Nothing is sent to an external system until you add a receiver.
default.example: Alerts are displayed on the Alerting UI

variants.defaultRationale: The postinstallation overview says firing alerts are displayed on the Alerting UI by default.

alternatives.label: Send alerts to an external receiver
alternatives.summary: You can add one or more receivers. The documented receiver types are PagerDuty, Webhook, Email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. The watchdog alert fires continuously so you can tell when delivery stops.
alternatives.example:
PagerDuty
Webhook
Email
Slack
Microsoft Teams

variants.prompt: After installation, how will users log in besides kubeadmin?

default.label: kubeadmin only
default.summary: No identityProviders entry. Add a provider before you rely on the cluster for other users.

variants.defaultRationale: Identity providers are configured after install on the OAuth cluster object. kubeadmin exists until you add a provider and remove it.

alternatives.label: HTPasswd
alternatives.summary: Validate users against an htpasswd file stored in a secret in openshift-config. The secret key must be named htpasswd.
alternatives.example:
kind: OAuth
name: cluster
type: HTPasswd
mappingMethod: claim
htpasswd.fileData.name: htpass-secret

alternatives.label: Keystone
alternatives.summary: Validate users against OpenStack Keystone.

alternatives.label: LDAP
alternatives.summary: Validate users against an LDAPv3 server with a simple bind. The sample attribute id is dn.
alternatives.example:
type: LDAP
mappingMethod: claim
ldap.attributes.id: dn

alternatives.label: Basic authentication
alternatives.summary: Validate users against a remote identity provider with a basic authentication URL.
alternatives.example:
name: basicidp
type: BasicAuth
mappingMethod: claim

alternatives.label: Request header
alternatives.summary: Identify users from a header such as X-Remote-User, usually set by an authenticating proxy. This provider cannot be combined with HTPasswd, Keystone, LDAP, or basic authentication.

alternatives.label: GitHub
alternatives.summary: Use a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise OAuth application.
alternatives.example:
name: githubidp
type: GitHub
mappingMethod: claim

alternatives.label: GitLab
alternatives.summary: Use GitLab OAuth. GitLab 11.1 and later can use OpenID Connect instead.

alternatives.label: Google
alternatives.summary: Use Google OpenID Connect.

alternatives.label: OpenID Connect
alternatives.summary: Use an OpenID Connect provider with the Authorization Code Flow.
alternatives.example:
name: oidcidp
type: OpenID
mappingMethod: claim

variants.prompt: After installation, will infrastructure workloads move onto dedicated nodes?

default.label: Keep workloads on the existing nodes
default.summary: Do not add the infra role. Registry, monitoring, and ingress keep their current placement.

variants.defaultRationale: Infrastructure nodes are optional. The postinstallation chapter uses them when you want to move infrastructure resources off the application nodes.

alternatives.label: Label infrastructure nodes
alternatives.summary: Label the compute nodes that should run infrastructure workloads, then taint them so only pods that tolerate the taint are scheduled there.
alternatives.example:
oc label node <node-name> node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=""
oc adm taint nodes node1 node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=reserved:NoSchedule

variants.prompt: Which update channel will this cluster follow?

default.label: stable-4.22
default.summary: A new cluster starts on the stable channel. Releases arrive after the fast channel, once regression data has been collected.

variants.defaultRationale: Newly installed clusters default to using stable channels.

alternatives.label: fast-4.22
alternatives.summary: Production clusters may use fast. Releases arrive when the errata is published.

alternatives.label: eus-4.y
alternatives.summary: The eus channel is offered for even-numbered minors, including 4.22, and is meant for Control Plane Only updates between EUS versions.

alternatives.label: candidate-4.22
alternatives.summary: You can switch to candidate at any time. Some releases on this channel are unsupported.

alternatives.label: Empty channel
alternatives.summary: Use an empty channel when the cluster cannot reach an update recommendation service, such as a restricted network with no local service.

variants.prompt: After installation, will etcd encrypt secret and config map values?

default.label: Leave etcd unencrypted
default.summary: The identity type is the default. Values in etcd are stored without encryption.

variants.defaultRationale: By default, etcd data is not encrypted. Encryption is an extra step after the cluster exists.

alternatives.label: AES-GCM
alternatives.summary: Encrypt secrets, config maps, routes, and OAuth tokens with AES-GCM. Keep the encryption keys with any etcd backup.

alternatives.label: AES-CBC
alternatives.summary: Encrypt the same resources with AES-CBC and PKCS#7 padding. Keys rotate every 7 days.

variants.prompt: Which worker latency profile fits the network between control plane and compute?

default.label: Default
default.summary: Kubelet posts node status every 10s. The controller manager waits 40s before marking a node unhealthy.

variants.defaultRationale: The Default profile is the starting configuration. Change it only when network latency is higher than usual.

alternatives.label: MediumUpdateAverageReaction
alternatives.summary: Use this when latency is slightly higher than usual. Kubelet updates every 20s and the controller manager waits 2m.

alternatives.label: LowUpdateSlowReaction
alternatives.summary: Use this when latency is extremely high. Move from Default to MediumUpdateAverageReaction first. A direct change from Default to this profile is not supported.

citations.locator: 4.4.2. Using and changing worker latency profiles
